To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

use of 40 kg N ha−1 in irrigation level after 50% available water depletion and nitroxin in irrigation level after available water depletion 50% and nitrogen combination in 75% available water depletion can increase biomass production, water use efficiency, nitrogen use efficiency, phosphorus uptake and nitrogen uptake in coneflowe.

the use of nitroxin in combination with nitrogen fertilizer and irrigation after 50–75% of available water in coneflower cultivation can lead to high biomass production with high nitrogen, water and nitrogen efficiency.

irrigation after 50 percent of soil water depletion in combination with 40 kg N ha−1 or 40 kg N + Nitroxin in the first and the second year of coneflower cultivation, respectively, resulted in higher bioyield, higher nitrogen use efficiency and higher water use efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of different nitrogen sources in coneflower cultivation under different irrigation regimes.
the use of nitrogen and nitrox in coneflower and the effect of these factors on water and nitrogen use efficiencies.
a new and innovative approach to the use of biological nitrogen and its combination with chemical nitrogen in order to reduce nitrogen losses and improve the efficiency of water and nitrogen use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
using 40 kg ha−N and nitroxin at irrigation levels following soil water depletion after 50% is recommended.
use of nitroxin as a biological nitrogen source can increase nitrogen use efficiency, water use efficiency and bioyield and decrease nitrate concentration in coneflower.
the highest biomass yield, nitrogen and water use efficiencies were obtained from the use of 40 and 80 kg N ha−−1 and nitroxin in irrigation after 75% of soil water content in coneflower.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of biological nitrogen and chemical fertilizer in coneflower production can improve the quality and yield of the crop and also reduce the environmental pollution and increase water and nitrogen use efficiencies.

use of biological nitrogen and chemical nitrogen combination in irrigation levels following 75% of available water in coneflower could be considered as a suitable management for increasing water and nitrogen use efficiencies.
the highest bio-yield, water and nitrogen efficiency was obtained from the use of nitroxin with nitrogen in irrigation after 75% of soil water deficit in coneflower cultivation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the highest bio yield with less nitrate and higher water and nitrogen efficiency were obtained using 40 kg ha−1 of chemical nitrogen and nitroxins in irrigation levels after 25%, and 50% and nitroxin, 80 kg ha− 1 nitrogen in irrigation after 75% soil depletion.
the combination of biological and chemical nitrogen can be used in coneflower cultivation in the region under investigation.
